questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'one'?
questions.explanation: Uno is the number 1. Before a masculine noun it shortens to un (un libro = one book); before a feminine noun it becomes una (una casa = one house).

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'two'?
questions.explanation: Dos is the number 2 and never changes form for gender: dos perros, dos mesas. Count with it: uno, dos, tres.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'three'?
questions.explanation: Tres is the number 3. Like dos, it is invariable - the same form works with masculine and feminine nouns: tres gatos, tres casas.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'four'?
questions.explanation: Cuatro is the number 4. Watch the spelling: it starts with cua-, the same root you see in cuarenta (40) and cuatrocientos (400).

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'five'?
questions.explanation: Cinco is the number 5. It shares its root with cincuenta (50) - both start with cinc-, because 50 is five tens.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'ten'?
questions.explanation: Diez is the number 10 and the anchor for the teens: once (11), doce (12), trece (13), catorce (14), quince (15).

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'red'?
questions.explanation: Rojo is a color adjective, so it agrees with its noun: el coche rojo, la casa roja, los libros rojos. Most color words ending in -o change this way.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'blue'?
questions.explanation: Azul does not change for gender (el mar azul, la casa azul), but it adds -es in the plural: ojos azules.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'green'?
questions.explanation: Verde works for both genders because it ends in -e: el libro verde, la puerta verde. Only the plural changes: verdes.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'yellow'?
questions.explanation: Amarillo agrees with its noun like other -o adjectives: el sol amarillo, la flor amarilla. The double l is pronounced like a y in most dialects.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'black'?
questions.explanation: Negro agrees in gender and number with its noun: el perro negro, la casa negra, los gatos negros.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'white'?
questions.explanation: Blanco agrees with its noun: el papel blanco, la casa blanca. It can also be a noun meaning the color white.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'mother'?
questions.explanation: Madre is feminine and takes la: la madre. The plural los padres means 'the parents' - the masculine plural covers both mother and father.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'father'?
questions.explanation: Padre is masculine: el padre. Remember that los padres (plural) usually means 'the parents', not just 'the fathers'.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'brother'?
questions.explanation: Hermano is the masculine form (el hermano); a sister is la hermana. Los hermanos can mean 'brothers' or 'siblings' in general.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'sister'?
questions.explanation: Hermana is the feminine form with la; the masculine is hermano. In this word pair the ending marks the gender: -o male, -a female.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'friend'?
questions.explanation: Amigo is a male friend (el amigo); a female friend is una amiga. The -o/-a ending marks the gender of the person.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'teacher'?
questions.explanation: Profesor is a male teacher; a female teacher is profesora. The stress falls on the last syllable: pro-fe-SOR, and it takes no written accent.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'student'?
questions.explanation: Estudiante works for any student - el estudiante or la estudiante; the article shows the gender. Words ending in -nte often work this way.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'school'?
questions.explanation: Escuela is feminine: la escuela. Most nouns ending in -a are feminine and take la - escuela, casa, mesa.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'house'?
questions.explanation: Casa is feminine: la casa, following the common -a pattern. Note that 'at home' is en casa, with no article.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'water'?
questions.explanation: Agua is a feminine noun, but in the singular it takes el for sound: el agua. Adjectives stay feminine: el agua fría.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'bread'?
questions.explanation: Pan is masculine: el pan. It is one of the shortest, most common food words in Spanish - un pan is a loaf or roll of bread.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'milk'?
questions.explanation: Leche is feminine: la leche. Nouns ending in -e can be either gender, so learn the article with the word: la leche, la noche, el día.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'dog'?
questions.explanation: Perro is the male or general word for dog (el perro); a female dog is la perra. The double rr is trilled.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'cat'?
questions.explanation: Gato is masculine (el gato); a female cat is la gata. The -o/-a pair pattern again: gato/gata, perro/perra.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'bird'?
questions.explanation: Pájaro (PA-ha-ro) is masculine: el pájaro. The written accent on the á is essential - it fixes the stress on the first syllable, and without it the word is misspelled.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'fish'?
questions.explanation: Pez is one syllable and masculine: el pez. Pez is a live fish; fish served as food on a plate is pescado.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'book'?
questions.explanation: Libro is masculine: el libro. Do not confuse it with la biblioteca (the library) - a libro is the book itself, and a biblioteca holds many libros.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'table'?
questions.explanation: Mesa is feminine: la mesa, following the common -a ending pattern. Poner la mesa means 'to set the table'.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'chair'?
questions.explanation: Silla is feminine: la silla. The ll is pronounced like a y in most dialects: SEE-ya.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'door'?
questions.explanation: Puerta is feminine: la puerta. Note the ue diphthong: PUER-ta, with the stress on the first syllable.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'window'?
questions.explanation: Ventana is feminine: la ventana. Learn it as the partner of puerta (door) - both are openings in a house, but they are different words.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'day'?
questions.explanation: Día is masculine despite ending in -a: el día. The written accent on the í is required, and día is one of the common exceptions to the '-a means feminine' pattern.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'night'?
questions.explanation: Noche is feminine: la noche. Greetings switch by time of day - buenas noches works both as 'good evening' (arriving) and 'good night' (leaving).

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'morning'?
questions.explanation: Mañana is spelled with ñ (an n with a tilde): la mañana. Mañana also means 'tomorrow', so 'mañana por la mañana' means 'tomorrow morning'.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'hello'?
questions.explanation: Hola is the universal greeting, used at any time of day. The h is silent: OH-la.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'goodbye'?
questions.explanation: Adiós carries a written accent on the o: a-DIOS. It is the standard goodbye; 'see you later' is hasta luego.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'thank you'?
questions.explanation: Gracias is the standard 'thank you'. The reply is de nada ('you are welcome'), literally 'of nothing'.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'thank you' is 'gracias' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'please'?
questions.explanation: Por favor is literally 'as a favor' (por = for). It works before or after a request: la cuenta, por favor = the check, please.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'please' is 'por favor' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'good morning'?
questions.explanation: Buenos días is the morning greeting, used until about noon. Días is masculine plural, so the adjective is buenos (not buenas) - and día keeps its written accent in the plural.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'good morning' is 'buenos días' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'good night'?
questions.explanation: Buenas noches works when arriving in the evening and when leaving at night. Noches is feminine plural, which is why the adjective is buenas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'good night' is 'buenas noches' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to eat'?
questions.explanation: Comer is a regular -er verb: yo como, tú comes, él come. Spanish infinitives end in -ar, -er, or -ir, and the ending tells you the conjugation pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to eat' is 'comer' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to drink'?
questions.explanation: Beber is a regular -er verb like comer: yo bebo, tú bebes. In much of Latin America, tomar is also commonly used for drinking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to drink' is 'beber' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to speak'?
questions.explanation: Hablar is a regular -ar verb: yo hablo, tú hablas. The -ar family is the largest verb group in Spanish, so this pattern is worth mastering first.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to speak' is 'hablar' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to live'?
questions.explanation: Vivir is a regular -ir verb: yo vivo, tú vives. The -ir verbs share most endings with -er verbs; the nosotros form is the giveaway (vivimos, not vivemos).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to live' is 'vivir' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to run'?
questions.explanation: Correr is a regular -er verb: yo corro, tú corres. The double r is trilled.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to run' is 'correr' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'to walk'?
questions.explanation: Caminar is a regular -ar verb: yo camino, tú caminas. It comes from el camino - the path or road you walk on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'to walk' is 'caminar' in Spanish.

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'big'?
questions.explanation: Grande works for both genders: el perro grande, la casa grande. Placed before a singular noun it often shortens to gran: un gran día (a great day).

questions.question: What is the Spanish word for 'small'?
questions.explanation: Pequeño is spelled with ñ: pe-QUE-nyo. It agrees with its noun: el perro pequeño, la casa pequeña. Written without the tilde ('pequeno'), it is misspelled.
